RISK
IMPORTANT: This is a Specified Investment Product (SIP) / Complex Product, not a fixed deposit.

You may
receive your principal back in a weaker alternate currency, resulting in a loss when converted back to your
base currency.

This product is NOT covered by the Singapore Deposit Insurance Corporation (SDIC), even
though it is issued by a bank.

Product Description
The DCI is a short-tenor (typically 1 to 3 months) FX-linked structured deposit denominated in a Base
Currency (USD) with an Alternate Currency (AUD).

In exchange for accepting FX conversion risk, the investor
earns an enhanced yield versus a plain USD fixed deposit.

At maturity, if the AUD/USD exchange rate is at or
above the pre-agreed Strike Rate, principal and enhanced yield are paid in USD.

At maturity, if the AUD/USD exchange rate is at or
above the pre-agreed Strike Rate, principal and enhanced yield are paid in USD.

If the exchange rate is below
the Strike Rate, principal and yield are converted and paid in AUD at the Strike Rate — the weaker currency
— which can result in a loss when the investor subsequently converts back to USD.

Investors who can accept receiving their principal back in AUD (the weaker currency scenario) without

Investors who do not need guaranteed access to these funds before maturity.
Key Risks
FX conversion risk: the investor may receive principal and yield in AUD at a rate worse than the market
rate at maturity, crystallising a loss versus the original USD amount.
No early redemption: funds are locked until maturity regardless of the investor's liquidity needs.
Not deposit insured: despite being issued by a bank, the product is not covered by SDIC.
Issuer credit risk: repayment depends on the issuing bank's solvency.
Complexity and rollover risk: investors who roll the DCI repeatedly may not fully appreciate cumulative
FX exposure over time.

IMPORTANT: This is a Specified Investment Product (SIP) / Complex Product.

You may lose some or all of
your invested capital.

This product is NOT principal-protected, is NOT a deposit, and is NOT covered by
the Singapore Deposit Insurance Corporation (SDIC).

It is generally suitable only for Accredited Investors,
Expert Investors, or Institutional Investors, or for Retail Investors who have passed the relevant Customer
Account Review / Customer Knowledge Assessment and provided a signed risk acknowledgement.

Product Description
The Note is a 3-year, non-principal-protected, autocallable structured note linked to the worst-performing of a
basket of three underlying assets (a global equity index, a broad commodities index, and a single
emerging-market currency pair).

tructured note linked to the worst-performing of a
basket of three underlying assets (a global equity index, a broad commodities index, and a single
emerging-market currency pair).

The Note pays a contingent coupon of up to 11.5% p.a. only if the
worst-performing underlying closes at or above its Coupon Barrier (60% of Initial Level) on the relevant
observation date.

The Note may be redeemed early (“autocalled”) if the worst-performing underlying closes at
or above its Initial Level on any observation date.

If not autocalled and the worst-performing underlying closes
below its Knock-In Barrier (55% of Initial Level) on the final valuation date, investors receive underlying-linked
physical or cash settlement that can be substantially below the amount invested, up to a total loss of principal.

Who Is This Product Designed For?

Sophisticated investors (Accredited / Expert / Institutional) with a Growth or Aggressive Growth risk

Investors who can bear total loss of the invested capital without impact on their essential financial needs.

Key Risks
Capital loss risk: investors may lose part or all of their invested principal; the coupon is not guaranteed.

Issuer credit risk: repayment depends on the Issuer's solvency; the Note is an unsecured obligation of the
Issuer.

Issuer credit risk: repayment depends on the Issuer's solvency; the Note is an unsecured obligation of the
Issuer.

Market/underlying risk: linked to three different, uncorrelated asset classes (equity, commodities, FX),
increasing the probability that at least one underlying breaches its barrier (“worst-of” structure).

Liquidity risk: no public secondary market; early redemption may not be available or may be at a
substantial discount.

Complexity risk: the payoff is non-linear and path-dependent; investors may not fully understand the
conditions under which capital is at risk.

Currency risk: underlying includes an emerging-market currency pair (USD/IDR), which can be highly
volatile.

Concentration risk: not diversified — a single adverse move in any one underlying determines the
worst-of outcome.

Investment Suitability, Risk Profiling & Product Due
Diligence Policy
Meridian Peak Wealth Partners (Singapore) Pte.

Ltd. — Private Wealth Management Division
Document Code
POL-INV-011 (Rev.

9)
Classification
Internal Use Only
1.

Purpose
This Policy governs how client risk profiles are determined and how they must be matched against product
risk ratings before any recommendation or sale, consistent with the Financial Advisers Act (FAA) and MAS
Notice on Recommendations on Investment Products (FAA-N16).

2.

Client Risk Profiling
Every client must complete a Risk Profile Questionnaire (RPQ) at onboarding and at least every 2 years,
resulting in a Risk Score from 1 (most conservative) to 10 (most aggressive) and a corresponding Risk Profile
category:
Risk Score
Risk Profile
Typical Objective
1 - 2
Conservative
Capital preservation; minimal tolerance for loss
3 - 4
Cautious
Modest growth with limited downside
5 - 6
Balanced
Growth and income; can tolerate moderate volatility
7 - 8
Growth
Capital growth; accepts meaningful short-term losses
9 - 10
Aggressive Growth
Maximum growth; accepts high volatility and illiquidity
3.

n tolerate moderate volatility
7 - 8
Growth
Capital growth; accepts meaningful short-term losses
9 - 10
Aggressive Growth
Maximum growth; accepts high volatility and illiquidity
3.

Product Risk Rating (Specified Investment Product / SRI Scale)
All products distributed by the firm are assigned a Summary Risk Indicator (SRI) from 1 (lowest risk) to 7
(highest risk) by the Product Due Diligence Committee before approval for sale.

Products rated SRI 6 or 7, or
otherwise classified as Specified Investment Products (SIPs) under MAS rules (e.g. structured notes,
derivatives-linked instruments, leveraged/inverse products), are classified as Complex Products.

4.

Sale of Complex Products — Mandatory Requirements
A Customer Account Review (CAR) / Customer Knowledge Assessment (CKA) must be completed and
passed before a first sale of any Complex Product to a Retail Investor.

Complex Products may only be recommended to clients with a Risk Score of 7 or above (Growth or
Aggressive Growth profile), UNLESS the client is an Accredited Investor, Expert Investor, or Institutional
Investor as defined under the Securities and Futures Act (SFA).

Growth or
Aggressive Growth profile), UNLESS the client is an Accredited Investor, Expert Investor, or Institutional
Investor as defined under the Securities and Futures Act (SFA).

Where a client's Risk Score is below 7 but the client independently instructs a purchase of a Complex
Product without a recommendation (execution-only), the RM must issue a written risk acknowledgement
and obtain the client's signed confirmation before the trade is executed.

No Complex Product may represent more than 20% of a Retail Investor's liquid net worth at the time of
sale, absent documented senior management exception.

All Complex Product sales require independent Compliance pre-trade sign-off.

5.

Ongoing Suitability Monitoring

RMs must review portfolio-level suitability at each periodic review (Section 3 of POL-KYC-004) and
immediately upon any change in client risk profile, financial circumstances, or investment objective.

A holding
that no longer matches the client's current Risk Profile must be flagged in the review record as a Suitability
Exception and escalated to Compliance within 5 business days.

1.

Purpose
This Policy sets out the minimum standards for identifying and verifying the identity of clients, assessing
source of wealth and source of funds, and performing ongoing due diligence, in line with the Monetary
Authority of Singapore (MAS) Notice SFA 04-N02 (Prevention of Money Laundering and Countering the
Financing of Terrorism — Capital Markets Intermediaries) and internal Group standards.

2.

Scope
Applies to all Relationship Managers (RMs), onboarding officers, and compliance staff involved in accepting
new individual, joint, corporate, or trust clients across the firm's Singapore, Hong Kong, and regional booking
centres.

3.

Client Risk Rating
Every client must be assigned a Client Risk Rating (CRR) of Low, Medium, or High at onboarding and
reviewed at the frequency below.

The CRR determines the due diligence tier applied.

4.

Mandatory Identification Documents
Individual clients: government-issued photo ID (passport / NRIC), proof of residential address dated
within 3 months.

Corporate / trust clients: constitutional documents, register of directors and shareholders, beneficial
ownership declaration down to natural persons holding 25% or more.

All clients: declaration of source of wealth and source of funds, with supporting documentary evidence for
High CRR clients (e.g. sale agreements, audited financial statements, dividend vouchers).

5.

Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs)
Clients, and their immediate family members and close associates, must be screened against PEP and
sanctions lists at onboarding and on an ongoing basis (minimum: daily automated screening against list
updates).

A PEP match automatically assigns High CRR and requires Senior Management approval prior to

6.

Cross-Border Booking Centre Clients
Where a client is resident in one jurisdiction (e.g.

Indonesia, India, Hong Kong) and assets are booked in
another (e.g.

Singapore), the onboarding team must additionally confirm: (i) the cross-border marketing and

solicitation rules of the client's home regulator have been observed (e.g.

Indonesia's OJK, India's RBI/SEBI
regulations on outward remittance and offshore investment); (ii) tax residency self-certification has been
obtained for Common Reporting Standard (CRS) purposes; and (iii) source of funds for the cross-border
transfer has been independently verified.

7.

Ongoing Monitoring
Transaction monitoring alerts must be cleared or escalated within 5 business days.

Client information (occupation, net worth, source of wealth) must be refreshed at the review frequency in
Section 3, or immediately upon a material trigger event (e.g. large unexplained inflow, adverse media,
change in employment).

Dormant accounts (no client-initiated activity for 12 months) are subject to reactivation KYC refresh
before further transactions are processed.

8.

Roles & Responsibilities
Relationship Manager: collects documentation, performs first-level assessment, escalates red flags.

Compliance (Onboarding Team): independently reviews and approves/rejects new accounts; maintains
PEP/sanctions screening.

Senior Management: approves onboarding of all High CRR clients and any PEP relationships.
